messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered: service=edge-lb-health (P1)
incident-bot: reason=multiple LB targets unhealthy in eu-west-1; symptom=TCP/TLS handshake failures; triggered_by=healthcheck-fail-count>5
pagerduty: Alarm: https://redwood.pagerduty.com/incidents/P123456 — Acknowledged by alice at 2026-03-15T09:12:03Z
alice: acked. jumping on it.
alice: quick summary — healthchecks showing TLS handshake 525/5xx starting 09:05 UTC, spike in customer errors from eu region. Not yet seeing full failover but weights started shifting to us-west automatically.
raj: @alice i'm on network infra. fetching LB target list...
raj: output:
```
$ infra-cli lb describe redwood-edge-eu
targets: t-123 unhealthy(5), t-124 healthy, t-125 unhealthy(6)
weights: pool-eu=40% -> pool-us=60% (auto-weight-shift triggered)
```
maria: seeing SNI alerts in proxy logs: "handshake failure: no certificate for client SNI 'app.customer.com'"
alice: that's weird, cert rotation happened yesterday but rollout was staged. @maria can you grep for cert serial mismatch?
maria: found mismatches on t-125 and t-123.
```
$ jq '.tls.certs[] | {target:.,serial: .serial}' pool.json
{"target":"t-123","serial":"0xA5..."}
{"target":"t-125","serial":"0xB1..."}
```
oncall-eu: @alice handed off from PD. i'll coordinate with ops and support.
oncall-eu: immediate mitigation plan: 1) pause auto-weight-shift 2) set manual weights back to preferred-eu 3) drain unhealthy targets 4) rollback staged cert
sre-lead: +1. prioritize rollback of cert rollout; that will stop SNI mismatches.
alice: rolling back cert on t-123,t-125 now.
alice: command:
```
$ infra-cli cert rollback --target t-123 --from-tag stable-2026-03-14
$ infra-cli cert rollback --target t-125 --from-tag stable-2026-03-14
```
alice: cert rollback triggered, watching healthchecks.
raj: pausing auto routing:
```
$ infra-cli routing policy update redwood-edge --auto-weighting false
```
raj: manual weight set:
```
$ infra-cli weights set --pool eu 90 --pool us 10
```
support-lead: notifying support channels and creating customer-impact doc, listing top 5 affected accounts. ETA to customers: 15-20m for DNS TTL propagation if caches had been updated.
support-lead: important: some CDNs cached the new LB weight via DNS due to TTL drift; need to advise customers about client retry/backoff.
alice: healthcheck status improving on t-123 and t-125 — TLS handshake errors dropping.
alice: curl test:
```
$ curl -v --resolve app.customer.com:443:34.68.10.12 https://app.customer.com/health
* Connected to app.customer.com (34.68.10.12) port 443
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Certificate verified
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```
maria: logs: no more "no certificate for client SNI" after rollback. good.
oncall-eu: I'm going to unpause auto-weighting after 30m of stable metrics, unless objections.
sre-lead: agree. leave manual weights for now and monitor token latency and 5xxs.
alice: PD note: incident acknowledged, escalation suppressed. Will keep PD incident open until we hit 30m stable.
incident-bot: PagerDuty update: incident P123456 — status=acknowledged; escalations paused.
support-lead: drafting customer message: short blurb + ETA + mitigation. pinging legal for wording.
alice: final check: edge proxy versions on t-123,t-125 match stable. cmd:
```
$ ssh ops@t-123 'redwood-proxy --version'
redwood-proxy 1.12.4+stable
```
oncall-eu: handing off to night oncall in 45m. @sre-lead will be primary for postmortem.
sre-lead: Opening postmortem ticket: PM-2026-03-15-EDGE-WEIGHT-ROLLBACK
support-lead: Customer impact estimate: ~1200 requests failed at peak (0.3% global, 4% eu region) affecting 18 customers; no data loss; retries succeeded after ~2s median.
alice: TL;DR: automated routing reacted to unhealthy targets that had a partial cert rollout; caused weight shift and transient errors. Root cause: cert rollout gating missed a canary check for SNI mapping. Mitigations: rollback cert, paused auto-weighting, restored manual weights, created additional gating for cert canary.
oncall-eu: closing notes: set alert: if auto-weight >50% shift within 2m, suppress auto-change and page infra-team instead of auto-weight.
alice: thanks everyone. I'll add runbook steps to incidents playbook.
support-lead: leaving updates in #customer-status and scheduled an outbound at +30m.
incident-bot: Incident P123456: resolved -> monitoring. Auto-close scheduled in 6h if stable.
